title: Measure compressed validation archives and define on-demand restoration scope
changes: Document a measured cold-archive proposal: keep current inputs available, compress completed retained artifacts individually, resolve declared archived inputs through coordinated restoration and retire bounded restored copies after use. Production archival and automatic restoration remain unimplemented.

Record the existing ext4 filesystem constraint and the required catalog, hash verification, staging, publication, uncompressed-space checks, consumer leases and interrupted-restore handling before historical trees can be replaced.
validation: Managed unit target/validation/units/cold-storage-assessment-_br49tbe PASS: seven complete files in four categories, tar.zst levels 3 and 6, all eight group/level content round trips match SHA256. Original source content, size, mode and mtime remain unchanged; runner input guards pass and temporary archives/restored copies were automatically removed.

Combined sample: 369.848 MiB original, 47.303 MiB at level 3 (87.210% smaller), 43.009 MiB at level 6 (88.371% smaller). Compression took 0.807/2.064 seconds and extraction plus writes 0.542/0.533 seconds, excluding hash verification.
Retained compression-result.json, command log, input guards and supplemental evidence under the managed unit. Exact measurement harness and sample selection match their protected-before hashes.
limitations: Nonrandom sample of three dataset JSON files, one Cargo archive, one executable and two Wine DLLs; it does not establish total-target savings or migration eligibility. Single local runs with possibly warm caches are not general performance guarantees.

No historical input replaced or removed, no production archive manager or automatic resolver installed, and no active tree compressed. The regular-file experiment does not verify full directory metadata, hard/symbolic links, full Wine prefixes, native Windows restoration, corruption recovery or concurrent consumers.
